section: Finance Commissions - mandate and key recommendations of the 13th, 14th, 15th and 16th
subsections: Finance Commission functions under Article 280 - what it does and does not do

accepted.s: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President under which Article of the Constitution?
accepted.x: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President under Article 280 of the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact constitutional Article associated with the institution.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission functions under Article 280 - what it does and does not do

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Finance Commission:
1. It is a quasi-judicial body.
2. It is constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier.
3. Its recommendations are legally binding on the Union Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Finance Commission is quasi-judicial and is constituted every fifth year or earlier. Its recommendations are advisory rather than legally binding.
accepted.tq: Split the statements by distinguishing constitutional status from the binding nature of recommendations.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission functions under Article 280 - what it does and does not do

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a duty of the Finance Commission under Article 280(3)?
o: Maintaining the income-expenditure accounts of the Union and State Governments
Recommending the distribution of the net proceeds of shareable taxes between the Centre and the States
Recommending principles governing grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of India
Recommending measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities
accepted.x: Maintaining government income-expenditure accounts is not a Finance Commission function. Its duties include tax devolution, grants-in-aid principles and augmentation of State funds for local bodies.
accepted.tq: Find the administrative accounting function that does not belong to the Finance Commission.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission functions under Article 280 - what it does and does not do

accepted.s: Which institution primarily deals with the sharing of GST revenue?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
accepted.x: GST revenue-sharing recommendations are dealt with through the GST Council, not as a function of the Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Use institutional discrimination to separate closely related fiscal bodies.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission functions under Article 280 - what it does and does not do

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT ordinarily a function of the Finance Commission?
o: Recommending measures relating to local-body finances
Recommending tax devolution between the Centre and the States
accepted.x: Plan and discretionary grants are not functions of the Finance Commission. Tax devolution, grants-in-aid and local-body-related fiscal measures fall within its constitutional mandate.
accepted.tq: Reject the option that confuses Finance Commission transfers with discretionary grants.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission functions under Article 280 - what it does and does not do

accepted.s: Under Article 281, the report of the Finance Commission is submitted to the President and is thereafter laid before:
o: The NITI Aayog for final acceptance
Parliament along with a memorandum explaining the action taken
The GST Council with the approval of the RBI
The Supreme Court with a report of the Attorney General
accepted.x: Article 281 requires the report to be laid before Parliament along with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken on the recommendations.
accepted.tq: Link the constitutional Article with the correct recipient and follow-up document.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission functions under Article 280 - what it does and does not do

accepted.s: Which statement best describes the status of Finance Commission recommendations?
o: They become enforceable only after approval by the Reserve Bank of India.
They are advisory, although the Rajamannar view held that they should not be rejected without compelling reasons.
They are automatically enforceable as judicial decrees.
They are binding only when approved by the GST Council.
accepted.x: Finance Commission recommendations are advisory. The Rajamannar view nevertheless stated that they should not be rejected without compelling reasons.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between advisory recommendations and legally enforceable decisions.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission functions under Article 280 - what it does and does not do

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Finance Commission)
a. First Finance Commission
b. Fourth Finance Commission
c. Tenth Finance Commission
d. Eleventh Finance Commission

List-II (Chairperson)
i. A.M. Khusro
ii. K.C. Neogy
iii. K.C. Pant
iv. P.V. Rajamannar

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The First, Fourth, Tenth and Eleventh Finance Commissions were chaired by K.C. Neogy, P.V. Rajamannar, K.C. Pant and A.M. Khusro respectively.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure chairperson pair and eliminate codes with mismatched commissions.
accepted.sec: Finance Commissions - chairpersons and award periods

accepted.s:
Match the following Finance Commissions with their chairpersons:

a. Twelfth Finance Commission
b. Thirteenth Finance Commission
c. Fourteenth Finance Commission
d. Fifteenth Finance Commission

i. N.K. Singh
ii. Vijay Kelkar
iii. C. Rangarajan
iv. Y.V. Reddy

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: C. Rangarajan chaired the Twelfth, Vijay Kelkar the Thirteenth, Y.V. Reddy the Fourteenth and N.K. Singh the Fifteenth Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Use the chairperson sequence to distinguish adjacent Finance Commissions.
accepted.sec: Finance Commissions - chairpersons and award periods

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the Finance Commission with its award period?
accepted.x: The Twelfth Finance Commission had the award period 2005–10. The Eleventh, Thirteenth and Fourteenth had award periods 2000–05, 2010–15 and 2015–20 respectively.
accepted.tq: Compare adjacent award periods rather than relying only on commission numbers.
accepted.sec: Finance Commissions - chairpersons and award periods

accepted.s: The Fourteenth Finance Commission was constituted on:
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission was constituted on 2 January 2013. The other dates relate to acceptance of its recommendations or constitution of later commissions.
accepted.tq: Match the exact constitution date with the correct Finance Commission.
accepted.sec: Finance Commissions - chairpersons and award periods

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sixteenth Finance Commission — constituted in November 2017 — N.K. Singh
Fifteenth Finance Commission — constituted in November 2017 — N.K. Singh
Fourteenth Finance Commission — constituted on 31 December 2023 — Y.V. Reddy
Sixteenth Finance Commission — constituted on 2 January 2013 — Arvind Panagariya
accepted.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission was constituted in November 2017 under the chairmanship of N.K. Singh. The Sixteenth was constituted on 31 December 2023 under Arvind Panagariya.
accepted.tq: Check both the constitution date and chairperson before accepting a pair.
accepted.sec: Finance Commissions - chairpersons and award periods

accepted.s: The award period of the Sixteenth Finance Commission is:
accepted.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission covers the period from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.
accepted.tq: Use the precise beginning and ending dates to distinguish the award period from earlier commissions.
accepted.sec: Finance Commissions - chairpersons and award periods

accepted.s:
Match the Finance Commission with the appropriate fact:

a. Fourteenth Finance Commission
b. Fifteenth Finance Commission
c. Sixteenth Finance Commission
d. Thirteenth Finance Commission

i. Arvind Panagariya as Chairperson
ii. Award apportioned between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana under the Reorganisation Act

iii. N.K. Singh as Chairperson
iv. Y.V. Reddy as Chairperson

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Fourteenth, Fifteenth and Sixteenth Finance Commissions were associated with Y.V. Reddy, N.K. Singh and Arvind Panagariya respectively. The Thirteenth Finance Commission award to undivided Andhra Pradesh was apportioned between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana under Section 46(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
accepted.tq: Use distinctive commission-specific facts to anchor the matching code.
accepted.sec: Finance Commissions - chairpersons and award periods

accepted.s: The Fourteenth Finance Commission’s recommendation of 42 per cent represented:
o: The largest-ever jump in the States’ share, by 10 percentage points
A continuation of the 32 per cent share without change
A temporary share applicable only to Union Territories
The first reduction in the States’ share of divisible taxes
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission increased the States’ share from 32 per cent to 42 per cent, an increase of 10 percentage points and the largest-ever jump mentioned here.
accepted.tq: Calculate the change between successive percentages instead of merely recalling the final figure.

accepted.s: The Fourteenth Finance Commission’s recommendation on States’ share of divisible taxes was accepted on:
accepted.x: The 42 per cent recommendation of the Fourteenth Finance Commission was accepted on 24 February 2015.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of acceptance from the dates of constitution of other commissions.

accepted.s: Which explanation was associated with the reduction of the States’ share from 42 per cent to 41 per cent under the Fifteenth Finance Commission?
o: Reduction in the number of States to 25
Jammu and Kashmir becoming a Union Territory
accepted.x: The one-percentage-point reduction was associated with Jammu and Kashmir becoming a Union Territory.
accepted.tq: Link a numerical change to the specific structural reason given for it.

accepted.s: The award of the Thirteenth Finance Commission to undivided Andhra Pradesh was apportioned between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana under:
o: Section 46(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014
accepted.x: Section 46(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided for apportionment using population ratio and other parameters.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact statutory provision rather than a related constitutional Article.

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the major compositional shift associated with the Fourteenth Finance Commission?
o: From grants towards tax devolution as the main route of transfers
From Finance Commission transfers to GST Council transfers alone
From tax devolution to only discretionary grants
From State transfers to monetary policy operations
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission treated tax devolution as the main route, marking a compositional shift from grants towards devolution.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of the policy shift by comparing the two transfer channels.

accepted.s: Which distinction was ended by the Fourteenth Finance Commission?
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission ended the distinction between Plan and non-Plan expenditure.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar expenditure classifications.

accepted.s: The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended local body grants of approximately:
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended local body grants of ₹2,87,436 crore, including ₹2,00,292 crore for Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total local-body grant from the rural-local-body amount and later totals.

accepted.s: Under the Fourteenth Finance Commission’s local-body grant framework, the allocation was based on which combination?
o: 2011 population at 90 per cent and area at 10 per cent, with basic and performance components
2011 population at 50 per cent and income distance at 50 per cent only
1971 population at 90 per cent and forest cover at 10 per cent, without performance grants
Area at 90 per cent and tax effort at 10 per cent, with only a basic grant
accepted.x: The grants were divided into basic and performance components and based on 2011 population at 90 per cent and area at 10 per cent.
accepted.tq: Apply several linked allocation rules to the local-body grant scenario.

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the Fourteenth Finance Commission’s criteria is correct?
o: Forest cover carried 50 per cent weight and area was excluded.
Population of 2011 carried 50 per cent weight and income distance was excluded.
Income distance carried 50 per cent weight and a 2 per cent floor was provided for small States.
Income distance carried 2 per cent weight and small States received no floor.
accepted.x: Income distance had a 50 per cent weight, and a 2 per cent floor was provided for small States.
accepted.tq: Match the criterion with both its weight and the associated special provision.

accepted.s:
Match the criterion with its weight under the Fourteenth Finance Commission:

a. Income distance
b. Population of 1971
c. Population of 2011
d. Area

i. 10 per cent
ii. 15 per cent
iii. 17.5 per cent
iv. 50 per cent

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission assigned 50 per cent to income distance, 17.5 per cent to 1971 population, 10 per cent to 2011 population and 15 per cent to area.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive 50 per cent income-distance pair and complete the code.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the criterion with its weight under the Fifteenth Finance Commission?
o: Forest cover and ecology — 2.5 per cent
accepted.x: Under the Fifteenth Finance Commission, income distance carried 45 per cent. Population of 2011, forest cover and ecology, and demographic performance carried 15, 10 and 12.5 per cent respectively.
accepted.tq: Reject altered percentages by comparing the full criterion table.

accepted.s: Under the Fifteenth Finance Commission, the weight assigned to tax and fiscal effort was:
accepted.x: Tax and fiscal effort carried a weight of 2.5 per cent under the Fifteenth Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Use the exact small percentage rather than confusing it with demographic performance or ecology.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the weights under the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Income distance 45 per cent, population of 2011 15 per cent and demographic performance 12.5 per cent
Income distance 42.5 per cent, area 15 per cent and tax effort 2.5 per cent
Income distance 50 per cent, population of 1971 17.5 per cent and tax effort 2.5 per cent
Income distance 42.5 per cent, population of 2011 17.5 per cent and contribution to GDP 10 per cent
accepted.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission assigned 42.5 per cent to income distance, 17.5 per cent to 2011 population and 10 per cent to contribution to GDP.
accepted.tq: Use the new GDP criterion and compare it with the altered weights of earlier commissions.

accepted.s: Which criterion was newly included by the Sixteenth Finance Commission with a weight of 10 per cent?
accepted.x: Contribution to GDP was a new criterion under the Sixteenth Finance Commission and carried a weight of 10 per cent.
accepted.tq: Identify the newly introduced criterion rather than a continuing one.

accepted.s: Which criterion was dropped under the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
accepted.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission dropped tax and fiscal effort as a criterion. Area, ecology and 2011 population continued with revised weights.
accepted.tq: Find the discontinued criterion by comparing successive columns.

accepted.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission provided grants for Rural Local Bodies amounting to approximately:
accepted.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission provided ₹2.36 lakh crore for Rural Local Bodies during 2021–26. The ₹1.18 lakh crore figure relates to the Fourteenth Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Separate successive commission amounts that are close in wording and subject.

accepted.s: Which statement regarding grants recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission is correct?
o: It recommended ₹1.5 lakh crore for Urban Local Bodies and total grants of ₹10.1 lakh crore including specified categories.
It recommended ₹3.56 lakh crore for Urban Local Bodies and total grants of ₹9.47 lakh crore.
It recommended no grants for Urban Local Bodies during 2021–26.
It recommended only revenue-deficit grants and excluded sector-specific grants.
accepted.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended ₹1.5 lakh crore for Urban Local Bodies and total grants of ₹10.1 lakh crore including revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Fifteenth Finance Commission grant figures from the corresponding Sixteenth Finance Commission figures.

accepted.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended ₹4,800 crore for the period 2022–23 to 2025–26 to incentivise States for:
accepted.x: An amount of ₹4,800 crore was recommended to incentivise States on educational outcomes during 2022–23 to 2025–26.
accepted.tq: Match the specific amount and time period with its policy objective.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sixteenth Finance Commission:
1. Its total grants were ₹9.47 lakh crore.
2. The share of grants in Finance Commission transfers fell from 19.4 per cent to 8.3 per cent.
3. Revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants were discontinued.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended total grants of ₹9.47 lakh crore, reduced the grants share from 19.4 per cent to 8.3 per cent and discontinued the three specified categories of grants.
accepted.tq: Check the total, percentage trend and discontinued categories together.

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the Sixteenth Finance Commission’s local-body grants?
o: Total local bodies — ₹7.91 lakh crore; rural — ₹4.35 lakh crore; urban — ₹3.56 lakh crore
Total local bodies — ₹9.47 lakh crore; rural — ₹7.91 lakh crore; urban — ₹1.55 lakh crore
Total local bodies — ₹4.35 lakh crore; rural — ₹3.56 lakh crore; urban — ₹7.91 lakh crore
Total local bodies — ₹7.91 lakh crore; rural — ₹1.55 lakh crore; urban — ₹4.35 lakh crore
accepted.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended ₹7.91 lakh crore for local bodies, comprising ₹4.35 lakh crore for rural bodies and ₹3.56 lakh crore for urban bodies.
accepted.tq: Check whether the component amounts add up to the stated total.

accepted.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission’s local-body grant recommendations, which statement is correct?
o: The urban share was 36 per cent and no wastewater component was specified.
The urban share rose to 45 per cent, with ₹56,100 crore for wastewater and ₹10,000 crore as an urbanisation premium.
The urban share fell to 10 per cent, with ₹10,000 crore for wastewater.
The entire local-body grant was assigned to urban bodies.
accepted.x: The urban component accounted for 45 per cent, up from 36 per cent. The package included ₹56,100 crore for wastewater and ₹10,000 crore as an urbanisation premium.
accepted.tq: Compare the changed urban share with the two earmarked components.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the disaster-related recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Disaster grants were ₹9.47 lakh crore, with no State corpus or new notified disasters.
Disaster grants were discontinued along with all local-body grants.
Disaster grants were ₹1.55 lakh crore, the State corpus was ₹2.04 lakh crore, and heatwaves and lightning were added as notified disasters.
Disaster grants were ₹56,100 crore and were limited to wastewater management.
accepted.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended ₹1.55 lakh crore in disaster grants and a State corpus of ₹2.04 lakh crore. Heatwaves and lightning were added as notified disasters.
accepted.tq: Combine the monetary figures with the new policy inclusions.

accepted.s: The cost-sharing ratio for disaster-related expenditure recommended for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States was:
accepted.x: The recommended cost-sharing ratio was 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and 75:25 for other States.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the special regional ratio from the general-State ratio.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Constitution of the Fifteenth Finance Commission
B. Constitution of the Fourteenth Finance Commission
C. Constitution of the Sixteenth Finance Commission
D. Acceptance of the Fourteenth Finance Commission’s 42 per cent devolution recommendation
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission was constituted on 2 January 2013, its recommendation was accepted on 24 February 2015, the Fifteenth was constituted in November 2017, and the Sixteenth was constituted on 31 December 2023.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the intermediate dates.
accepted.sec: Finance Commissions - chairpersons and award periods

accepted.s: The report of the Sixteenth Finance Commission was submitted and tabled, respectively, on:
accepted.x: The report was submitted on 17 November 2025 and tabled on 1 February 2026.
accepted.tq: Preserve the order of submission and tabling dates.

accepted.s: Which of the following was accepted by the Union Government in relation to the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Continuation of all revenue-deficit and State-specific grants without modification
The recommendation on devolution, with Finance Commission grants of ₹1.4 lakh crore for 2026–27
The 50 per cent States’ share demanded by 18 States
A reduction of the States’ share from 41 per cent to 32 per cent
accepted.x: The Centre accepted the devolution recommendation, and Finance Commission grants of ₹1.4 lakh crore were provided for 2026–27.
accepted.tq: Match the accepted recommendation with its associated annual grant figure.

accepted.s: Under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, the Finance Commission consists of:
o: Five members elected by the States
A Chairman and two members appointed by Parliament
A Chairman and four members appointed by the President
A Chairman, four members and the RBI Governor appointed by the Union Cabinet
accepted.x: The Finance Commission comprises a Chairman and four members appointed by the President, in accordance with Article 280(1).
accepted.tq: Check both the composition and appointing authority.
accepted.sec: Composition and qualifications - FC (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1951

accepted.s: Which of the following qualifications is prescribed for the Chairman of the Finance Commission?
o: Prior membership of the GST Council
Mandatory service as a sitting High Court judge
Service as Governor of a State
accepted.x: The Chairman must have experience in public affairs. The other positions are not prescribed as mandatory qualifications for the Chairman.
accepted.tq: Identify the statutory qualification without importing qualifications of other members.
accepted.sec: Composition and qualifications - FC (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1951

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the categories from which members of the Finance Commission may be selected under the prescribed qualifications?
o: A person who is or has been, or is qualified to be, a judge of a High Court
A person having wide experience in financial matters and administration
A person having mandatory experience as a monetary policy committee member
A person having special knowledge of Government finance and accounts
accepted.x: The prescribed categories include a High Court judge or qualified person, a Government finance and accounts expert, a person with financial and administrative experience, and an economics expert. Mandatory Monetary Policy Committee experience is not listed.
accepted.tq: Find the qualification borrowed from a different financial institution.
accepted.sec: Composition and qualifications - FC (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1951

accepted.s:
Which combination correctly represents the prescribed areas of expertise for Finance Commission members?
1. Government finance and accounts
2. Financial matters and administration
3. Economics
4. Monetary policy operations as a compulsory qualification
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Special knowledge of Government finance and accounts, wide experience in financial matters and administration, and special knowledge of economics are prescribed areas. Compulsory experience in monetary policy operations is not prescribed.
accepted.tq: Separate the listed statutory qualifications from an unrelated financial-sector qualification.
accepted.sec: Composition and qualifications - FC (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1951

accepted.s: A person who has served as a member of the Finance Commission can be appointed again to the Commission. This reflects which provision?
o: Members are elected by the States for two consecutive terms
Members automatically become members of the GST Council
accepted.x: The prescribed provisions make members eligible for reappointment. They do not provide for lifetime tenure or automatic membership of another body.
accepted.tq: Apply the statutory rule to a reappointment situation.
accepted.sec: Composition and qualifications - FC (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1951
